definitions.explanation: The process of solid particles settling to the bottom of a liquid due to gravity. Also refers to the sediment itself.

examples.japanese: {沈殿物|ちんでんぶつ}を{取|と}り{除|のぞ}く
{砂|すな}が{底|そこ}に{沈殿|ちんでん}した。
{化学|かがく}{反応|はんのう}によって{白|しろ}い{沈殿|ちんでん}が{生|しょう}じた。
examples.english: A white precipitate formed from the chemical reaction.

notes:
USAGE: Primarily a scientific/technical term used in chemistry, physics, and environmental science. The noun form {沈殿物|ちんでんぶつ} refers to the settled material (sediment/precipitate).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {沈殿物|ちんでんぶつ} (sediment, precipitate)
- {沈殿|ちんでん}{反応|はんのう} (precipitation reaction)
- {沈殿|ちんでん}する (to settle, precipitate)
- {底|そこ}に{沈殿|ちんでん}する (to settle at the bottom)

RELATED WORDS:
- {堆積|たいせき} (accumulation, sedimentation - geological)
- {沈澱|ちんでん} (alternative kanji for same word)
- {浮遊|ふゆう} (floating, suspension - opposite state)
